problem: MLLM-based VLN agents (NaVid, StreamVLN, NaVILA) feed dense RGB patch tokens from all historical frames to the model. This creates heavy token redundancy and high compute, and the tokens carry no explicit spatial structure or multi-view geometric consistency. They also typically rely on DAgger augmentation and VQA co-training.
motivation: Navigation is mostly constrained to the ground plane, so a compact agent-centric BEV layout should preserve the needed spatial information at far lower token cost. Depth-projected features give explicit geometry, and 3D foundation models such as VGGT supply learned multi-view structural priors that are robust when depth is noisy. Combining both could improve spatial reasoning and efficiency without extra data-generation pipelines.
key_idea: Replace dense historical RGB tokens with a compact agent-centric BEV token map built by depth-projecting both SigLIP patch features and VGGT features into 3D, then mean-pooling them per BEV grid cell before feeding an MLLM.
insight: BEV compression alone cuts visual tokens from 4003 to 394 and improves SR from 46.49 to 51.50 (w/o SRDF). Adding VGGT features gives a further gain (53.56 SR, 514 tokens), so explicit and implicit geometry are complementary. Naively concatenating depth as extra image tokens doubles the tokens and hurts (SR 38.61), so how depth is used matters. Global mean pooling beats hierarchical per-modality pooling, a 0.25 m grid is the best trade-off, and a history longer than about 48 steps gives no gain.
method: Explicit depth-guided projection: resize depth to the patch grid (bicubic), back-project each patch center to a 3D world point with the pinhole model, camera intrinsics K and pose [R|p], and transform history into the current ego frame.

Implicit 3D priors: run frozen VGGT-1B on the historical frames, take penultimate-layer features, map them with a 2-layer MLP (4096 hidden) to the SigLIP dimension, and project them into 3D with the same depth procedure.

Grid-based BEV aggregation: discretize the (x,z) plane into cells of 0.25 m over a [-10,10] m range, mean-pool all SigLIP and VGGT features in a cell, add a 2D sinusoidal position embedding, and keep only non-empty cells as tokens.
MLLM policy: LLaVA-Video-7B receives the instruction, the BEV tokens (built from up to 8 historical observations) and the current front-view image tokens, and predicts 4 discrete actions per round.
Two-round dialogue (StreamVLN-style): the second round reuses the BEV and only adds the new frame, so BEV is updated once every 8 actions; STOP terminates.

Training: fine-tune everything except VGGT on navigation data only (R2R-CE, RxR-CE, EnvDrop, ScaleVLN, SRDF), for 2 epochs, with no DAgger and no VQA; NavRAG-CE results come from 1 extra fine-tuning epoch.

setting.backbone: LLaVA-Video-7B (fine-tuned) with SigLIP encoder + frozen VGGT-1B + MLP projector
setting.training_data: Navigation data only: R2R-CE 10,819 traj, RxR-CE 19,990, EnvDrop 146,304, ScaleVLN 155,098, SRDF 319,022 (converted to continuous, filtered); no DAgger, no VQA; NavRAG-CE fine-tuning for 1 epoch for that benchmark
setting.observation: Monocular front-facing RGB (60° FoV) + depth + pose/odometry
setting.action_space: Low-level discrete: forward 0.25 m / turn left / turn right / STOP (4 actions per round)
setting.privileged: none (uses depth and pose/odometry, which are standard sensor inputs)

numbers.extra: Trained on nav data incl. SRDF/ScaleVLN/EnvDrop; no DAgger, no VQA
numbers.evidence: Table 1 comparison with SOTA on R2R-CE, RxR-CE, NavRAG-CE val_unseen, row Ours

BEV only, no 3D foundation model features

results: GA-VLN reaches 61.0 SR / 55.2 SPL on R2R-CE val-unseen, beating InternVLA-N1 (58.2 / 54.0) and StreamVLN (56.9 / 51.9) without DAgger. On RxR-CE it gets 55.4 SR, beating InternVLA-N1 (53.5), though SPL 45.2 is below 46.1. It also cuts inference from 32.19 to 8.73 TFLOPs and latency from 342.9 to 258.7 ms versus its RGB-token baseline.
limitations: Real-world tests are qualitative only, run without obstacle avoidance; the agent hugs walls and stops imprecisely.
On NavRAG-CE SR/SPL trail Dynam3D (22.2/18.2 vs 24.7/18.8), and mixing NavRAG data into training hurts R2R-CE/RxR-CE.
Requires depth and accurate pose, plus a heavy frozen VGGT-1B; performance degrades under rotation noise (SR 58.29).
